name: Benin
summary_text: Benin is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal, but 76crimes documents that anti-gay lynchings are commonplace; the Hirondelles Club provides safe housing for LGBT youth fleeing family violence. No LGR, no anti-discrimination law; community organises underground.

sources.title: Help for LGBT youths in Benin, where anti-gay lynchings are commonplace
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (April 2024): interview with Luc Agblakou, founder of the Hirondelles Club in Benin, which since 2013 has supported LGBT+ people with housing - founded after a father murdered his gay son. Nearly 380 young people from Benin and the sub-region have passed through its 20-place temporary accommodation centre; the organisation now has branches in Togo, Burkina Faso and Niger. Article notes anti-gay lynchings are commonplace in Benin.

sources.title: Benin | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations are not criminalised in Benin, but there is no SOGISC discrimination protection, no legal gender recognition, and LGBTI organisations cannot register. LGBTIQ people face stigma from the public and police, which cracked down on a 'network of homosexuals' in 2022. The 2021 Benin Human Rights Commission report flagged physical and sexual assault, arbitrary detention, torture and degrading treatment against LGBTQI+ people; LBQ women rarely report violence to police.

sources.title: Benin - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Benin: official assessment including the section on acts of violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity - same-sex conduct not criminalised but no protections; documents societal stigma and police treatment.

sources.title: Voices from LGBT Catholics in Western Africa
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Aug 2015): 'Voices from LGBT Catholics in Western Africa' — faithful in Ghana, Togo, Benin and Nigeria describe persecution and discrimination within the church and society.

sources.title: What traditional African homosexuality learned from West
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (May 2012): interview with anthropologist Patrick Awondo - homosexuality has a long history in Africa (evidence in Cameroon, Zimbabwe, Burkina Faso and Benin, including Mossi kings' relations with pages and marriages between women in Dahomey); colonial-era laws and anti-discrimination activism are the Western imports.
